- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, model tends to under-forecast sharp upward moves; adjust upward by 2–5% for early spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and forecast is rising, model often over-optimistically extrapolates; cap upward momentum at 1–3% above recent peak.
- After a strong upward spike (e.g., >10% from prior 30d avg), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–7% in next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00) and history shows volatility, model tends to smooth out noise; increase forecast variance by 1–2% to reflect true range.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, model exhibits mean reversion bias; reduce next forecast by 2–4% to align with recent mean.
- For 30d forecasts, if last 3–5 days of true values show downward trend, model often ignores it; add 1–3% downward bias to next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history includes 0.50 (strong bullish), model often over-anticipates; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
